summary: Unexpected routing to legacy CPU quantized variant resulting in large p99 spikes and intermittent timeouts
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports a sudden increase in tail latency and intermittent 504 timeouts starting 2026-03-09 22:00 UTC. Traffic for production model alias 'neuroplan-summaries-v2' was observed routing to an older CPU-quantized variant (open-llm-13b-q4_legacy_cpu) that is not part of the normal warm-up pool. The legacy variant is cold, single-replica, and has significantly higher per-token latency compared to the GPU-backed variants.

Impact:
- Several API calls from the customer's production workload experienced p99 latency ~8.5s and a 504 rate of ~3.2% over a 30-minute window.
- Customer-visible timeouts for summary generation in user-facing flows.
- Customer temporarily throttled traffic and reported revenue impact on downstream features.

Environment:
- Customer: NeuroPlan (dedicated)
- Model alias: neuroplan-summaries-v2
- Observed variants: open-llm-13b-q4 (gpu-optimized), open-llm-13b-q4_legacy_cpu (cpu-quantized, legacy)
- Region: prod/us-east (us-east-1)
- Traffic profile: bursty batch of short prompts 2026-03-09 21:50 - 22:30 UTC

Steps to reproduce (as-observed):
1) Customer sends high-concurrency bursts (~200 rps for 30s) to /v1/generate using alias neuroplan-summaries-v2.
2) Routing service selects target variant based on policy (cost-aware + capacity).
3) During burst window, some subset of requests are routed to the legacy CPU variant which has no prewarmed replicas.
4) Requests routed to that variant show large queuing and cold-start initialization before returning responses or timing out.

Observed logs and traces (examples):
- Sample request-id: req_20260309_us_91f2; trace-id: trace-0a7b; routed_variant: open-llm-13b-q4_legacy_cpu; start: 2026-03-09T22:05:11.423Z; first-byte: 2026-03-09T22:05:18.912Z; status: 504 (gateway timeout)
- K/V cache miss region: consistent for CPU variant; warmup-pool-size: 0 for legacy variant
- Autoscaler events: attempted scale for gpu pool was saturated; fallback policy invoked at 2026-03-09T22:03:47Z

Initial investigation notes:
- Routing policy evaluation: there is a new cost-aware weighting change (PR #820) rolled 2026-03-09 that included a heuristic fallback ordering which mistakenly treated the legacy CPU variant as a compatible low-cost alternative for short prompt workloads.
- The legacy variant does not have prewarm replicas configured (historical artifact), and warmup behavior requires cold container initialization plus model mmap, which adds ~4-6s overhead.
- Autoscaler reported spike on GPU pool and returned 'no capacity' and routing-service incorrectly allowed fallback to variants that are flagged as 'legacy' but still marked compatible in the variant-compatibility table.
- Trace sampling shows that requests hitting the legacy variant have high tail latencies; requests hitting GPU variants show normal latency (~220ms p99 during the same window).

Hypothesis:
1) The cost-weighting change made the routing policy prefer cheaper CPU variants when GPU capacity is reported as constrained; however, it failed to check 'warmup_pool_size' and 'prewarm_enabled' flags before routing.
2) Legacy CPU variant is not suitable as a low-latency fallback and should be excluded from automatic fallback chains unless explicitly pinned by customer.

Immediate customer-facing mitigation applied:
- Support instructed customer to pin alias neuroplan-summaries-v2 to the gpu-optimized variant until a fix is deployed. Customer applied pin at 2026-03-10T01:12Z which reduced errors immediately.
- Temporarily increased GPU reserved burst capacity for NeuroPlan while root cause is addressed.

Next steps planned:
- Engineering to add additional gating checks in routing-service to exclude variants with prewarm_enabled == false from automatic fallback chains. (Assigned to routing team)
- Add a deprecation/legacy flag that prevents routing-policy from treating legacy variants as compatible unless explicitly allowed by customer alias config.
- Expand observability to include variant warmup pool size in routing decision logs and dashboards.
- Postmortem and customer communications draft (CS to coordinate).

2026-03-10 03:05 - Diego Rivera (SRE): Confirmed traces showing routing to open-llm-13b-q4_legacy_cpu. Observed missing prewarm replicas for that variant in dedicated pool. Marking as In Progress and engaging routing team.

2026-03-10 07:22 - Priya Nair (Routing Eng): Found change in PR #820 that altered fallback candidate ranking. Adding guard to exclude variants flagged as legacy or prewarm_disabled. Will open a fix PR and run canary in staging. Linked PR: github.com/redwood-inference/routing-service/pull/845

2026-03-11 11:40 - Diego Rivera (SRE): Deployed hotfix in staging; test replay of burst traffic shows no routing to legacy CPU variant and tail latencies within expected bounds. Preparing rollout to prod with monitoring thresholds.

investigation_summary: Root cause appears to be a routing-policy regression introduced by a cost-weighting change that did not respect 'prewarm_enabled' or legacy status. When GPU capacity reported constrained, routing-service fell back to a legacy CPU variant that lacks warm replicas, causing cold-start overheads and elevated p99 latency. Autoscaler pressure on GPU pool triggered the fallback path. Engineering reproduced in staging and implemented a gating fix to block non-prewarmed variants from automatic fallback. A follow-up will add an explicit legacy flag to variant metadata and surface warmup pool size in routing logs.
resolution_notes: Workaround: Customer pinned alias to GPU variant and we increased reserved burst capacity temporarily. Permanent fix: routing-service PR #845 adds gating logic to exclude prewarm_disabled or legacy variants from auto-fallback; PR #847 adds variant metadata flag 'legacy_block' and updates compatibility table validation. Monitoring: added dashboard panels for variant warmup_pool_size, and routing decision logs include the prewarm_enabled check. Rollout: staged canary deployed 2026-03-11 and full rollout scheduled 2026-03-12 22:00 UTC. Customer notified 2026-03-12 10:00 UTC with planned rollout ETA.
follow_up_actions: Add automated alert when routing-service proposes fallback candidates that have warmup_pool_size == 0
Run a one-week audit of variant metadata to identify other legacy variants without prewarm configuration
Update docs/console UI to display 'prewarm_enabled' on variant config page
Customer outreach: account manager to provide formal incident summary and credit if SLA breach is confirmed
